title: Have the military support DHS border protection
proposal: The Defense Department should provide needed support to Department of Homeland Security border protection operations, which the chapter calls a national security issue.
quote: Provide necessary support to Department of Homeland Security (DHS) border protection operations.

title: Focus defense planning on China and defending Taiwan
proposal: U.S. defense planning and all defense efforts should focus on China, especially on being able to deny a Chinese takeover of Taiwan.
quote: U.S. defense planning should focus on China and, in particular, the effective denial defense of Taiwan.

title: Plan forces to defeat a Chinese invasion of Taiwan first
proposal: The military's conventional force planning should put defeating a Chinese invasion of Taiwan ahead of other missions, such as fighting a second war at the same time.
quote: Prioritize the U.S. conventional force planning construct to defeat a Chinese invasion of Taiwan before allocating resources to other missions

title: Make allied burden-sharing central to defense strategy
proposal: The United States should make allies taking more responsibility for their own defense a central part of its strategy and strongly push them to do so.
quote: Make burden-sharing a central part of U.S. defense strategy with the United States not just helping allies to step up, but strongly encouraging them to do so.

title: Build a collective defense with Taiwan, Japan and Australia
proposal: The U.S. should support more defense spending and cooperation by Taiwan and Asia–Pacific allies like Japan and Australia to form a shared defense model.
quote: Support greater spending and collaboration by Taiwan and allies in the Asia–Pacific like Japan and Australia to create a collective

title: Shift NATO conventional defense to Europe and cut U.S. troops there
proposal: NATO should change so European allies provide most of the conventional forces to deter Russia, relying on the U.S. mainly for nuclear deterrence, while the U.S. reduces its forces in Europe.
quote: Transform NATO so that U.S. allies are capable of fielding the great majority of the conventional forces required to deter Russia

title: Keep supporting Israel; have Gulf partners handle their own defenses
proposal: The U.S. should keep supporting Israel while helping Gulf partners take responsibility for their own coastal, air, and missile defenses.
quote: Sustain support for Israel even as America empowers Gulf partners to take responsibility for their own coastal, air, and missile defenses

title: Let South Korea lead its own conventional defense
proposal: South Korea should take the lead in its conventional (non-nuclear) defense against North Korea.
quote: Enable South Korea to take the lead in its conventional defense against North Korea.

title: Expand and modernize the U.S. nuclear arsenal
proposal: The U.S. should expand and modernize its nuclear forces, including new theater-level capabilities, so it can deter Russia and China at the same time.
quote: Expand and modernize the U.S. nuclear force so that it has the size, sophistication, and tailoring to deter Russia and China simultaneously.

title: Have allies lead counterterrorism in their regions
proposal: The U.S. should keep counterterrorism forces at a sustainable cost and focus on building allies' and partners' ability to lead the fight against terrorism in their regions.
quote: Prioritize enhancing the capability of allies and partners to take the lead in combating terrorism in their regions.

title: Shift funding to flexible defense innovation organizations
proposal: The Pentagon's budget process should give more money and authority to mission-focused innovation groups instead of locked-in, program-specific budgets.
quote: Enhance funding and authority for DOD mission-focused innovation organizations and away from program-specific stovepipes

title: Act on the PPBE Reform Commission's recommendations
proposal: The President should review the congressionally mandated Commission on PPBE Reform's recommendations and plan to carry out those the administration supports.
quote: The President should examine the recommendations of the congressionally mandated Commission on Planning, Programming, Budgeting, and Execution

title: Fund emerging-tech prototypes outside the normal budget cycle
proposal: The administration should seek laws or other ways to fund testing of key new technologies outside the regular defense budget process, possibly with a 'fast track' for urgent needs.
quote: Develop legislation or other means of providing funding outside the traditional PPBE process for the prototyping and experimentation of emerging technologies

title: Hold 'Night Court' to end outdated weapons programs
proposal: Defense under secretaries and service secretaries should review programs ('Night Court'), end outdated or underperforming ones, and report results to the Secretary each year.
quote: conduct “Night Court” and use existing authorities to terminate outdated or underperforming programs so that money can be used for what works and will work.

title: Study how adversaries buy weapons faster
proposal: The Office of the Secretary of Defense should research and report on how rival nations acquire and field new technology faster.
quote: Require the Office of the Secretary of Defense to research and report on the acquisition processes used by America’s adversaries

title: Refill weapons stockpiles drawn down for Ukraine
proposal: The U.S. should replenish and maintain stockpiles of ammunition and equipment used up by U.S. support to Ukraine.
quote: Replenish and maintain U.S. stockpiles of ammunition and other equipment that have been depleted as a result of U.S. support to Ukraine.

title: Work with industry on a list of defense acquisition reforms
proposal: The Pentagon should work with industry to create a ranked list of reforms DOD and Congress could adopt to encourage companies to help the military innovate.
quote: Collaborate with industry to develop a prioritized list of reforms that the DOD and Congress can enact and implement

title: Expand multiyear weapons contracts and block buys
proposal: Defense buyers should have more ability to use multiyear contracts and bulk purchases to give contractors steadier returns and reduce overhead.
quote: Strengthen the ability of acquisition authorities to engage in multiyear procurements and block buys.

title: Favor U.S. and allied production under Buy America rules
proposal: Defense purchasing should prioritize the U.S. and allies under the Build America, Buy America Act and address loopholes that let items be made overseas.
quote: Prioritize the U.S. and allies under the “domestic end product” and “domestic components” requirements of the Build America, Buy America Act

title: Review which industries to bring back home or to allies
proposal: DOD should review the list of manufacturing sectors chosen for onshoring or 'friendshoring' and expand or change it based on strategic needs.
quote: Review the sectors currently prioritized for onshoring or “friendshoring” of manufacturing

title: Help small defense businesses grow
proposal: DOD should help small businesses grow into larger vendors with private customers too, and do more outreach to tell them about defense needs.
quote: Help small businesses to become medium-size and large vendors, which encourages a more resilient industrial base and fosters competition.

title: Reward fast acquisition decisions and skip needless rules
proposal: DOD should create incentives for fast decisions on starting and ending programs and let acquisition officials bypass unnecessary internal regulations while staying within the law.
quote: Create incentives to emphasize speed and agility in decision-making for prototyping and program-of-record starts and terminations.

title: Assess acquisition workforce needs
proposal: Defense under secretaries and service secretaries should assess their acquisition workforces and plan for the extra staff, resources, and training needed.
quote: should assess their acquisition workforces; determine what additional personnel, resources, and training they need; and develop implementation plans.

title: Open up acquisition training beyond Defense Acquisition University
proposal: DOD should decentralize Defense Acquisition University courses and let it accredit outside schools to train acquisition professionals.
quote: Decentralize Defense Acquisition University (DAU) offerings and expand the DAU mission to include accreditation of non-DOD institutions.

title: Increase DOD collaboration with labs and private companies
proposal: DOD should work more closely with government labs, private companies, and the wider tech community to solve hard problems and deploy new technology.
quote: Increase integration and collaboration among the DOD, government labs, and private companies to solve the department’s most difficult problems.

title: Cut the number of critical technology areas
proposal: DOD should reduce its list of 14 critical technology areas to a smaller number tied directly to great-power competition.
quote: Reduce the number of critical technology areas from 14 to a more manageable number to concentrate effort and resources

title: Rebuild old military research and testing facilities
proposal: DOD should rebuild research, development, and testing infrastructure housed in Cold War–era facilities.
quote: Rebuild RDT&E infrastructure that resides in Cold War–era facilities and is not well-suited to the current era of rapid development

title: Speed prototyping and build a China-focused tech pipeline
proposal: DOD should speed up prototyping for battlefield needs and set up a pipeline of near-, mid-, and long-term technologies aimed at competing with China.
quote: Establish a pipeline of near-term, mid-term, and long-term technology that is aimed at great-power competition (China)

title: Protect defense research from foreign theft
proposal: DOD should adopt a full plan to protect U.S. technology from theft, tailored to universities, industry, and labs, with consequences for attempted or actual theft.
quote: Implement a comprehensive approach to preserving U.S. technological leadership that is based on outpacing our adversaries

title: Design weapons for export from the start
proposal: Military leaders should plan for exportability when developing new systems, with a funding mechanism that is paid back through later foreign sales.
quote: Create a funding mechanism to incentivize exportability in initial planning, which can be recouped after future FMS transactions.

title: End informal congressional 'tiered review' of arms sales
proposal: The informal practice of previewing arms sales to Congress before formal notice should end, or be used only when unanimous support is certain, to speed foreign military sales.
quote: End the tiered review process to eliminate at least 20 days from the FMS process.

title: Loosen arms export rules (ITAR) for close allies
proposal: The U.S. should reduce International Traffic in Arms Regulations to make defense trade easier with allies such as the UK, Canada, and Australia.
quote: Decrease International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) to facilitate trade with such allies as the United Kingdom, Canada, and Australia.

title: Fund more contracting staff to speed foreign arms sales
proposal: All services should immediately get more contracting capacity, and arms sales decisions should be streamlined, to shorten the roughly 18-month foreign military sales contracting time.
quote: Immediately fund more contracting capacity in all services to decrease the contracting timeline and improve the delivery of defense articles

title: Name a White House aide for military recruiting
proposal: The President should appoint a Special Assistant to work with Congress, DOD, and others on military recruiting and retention.
quote: Appoint a Special Assistant to the President who will maintain liaison with Congress, DOD, and all other interested parties on the issue of recruiting and retention.

title: Suspend MHS Genesis medical record checks for recruits
proposal: DOD should stop using the MHS Genesis system at military entrance stations, which uses recruits' private medical records and, the chapter says, causes delays and wrongful rejections.
quote: Improve recruiting by suspending the use of the recently introduced MHS Genesis system that uses private medical records of potential recruits

title: Require the military aptitude test in federally funded schools
proposal: Recruiters should get more access to high schools, and all students in schools receiving federal money should be required to take the ASVAB military entrance exam.
quote: Improve military recruiters’ access to secondary schools and require completion of the Armed Services Vocational Aptitude Battery

title: Give recruiters time at congressional town halls
proposal: Members of Congress should be encouraged to give military recruiters time at each town hall in their districts.
quote: Encourage Members of Congress to provide time to military recruiters during each townhall session in their congressional districts.

title: Add more Junior ROTC programs
proposal: The number of Junior ROTC programs in high schools should be increased.
quote: Increase the number of Junior ROTC programs in secondary schools.

title: End enlistment exceptions for HIV and gender dysphoria
proposal: Exceptions that let people who need ongoing medical treatment, such as those who are HIV positive or have gender dysphoria, join the military should be removed.
quote: Exceptions for individuals who are already predisposed to require medical treatment (for example, HIV positive or suffering from gender dysphoria) should be removed

title: Remove transgender service members from the military
proposal: People with gender dysphoria should be expelled from military service, and policies allowing transgender people to serve should be reversed.
quote: and those with gender dysphoria should be expelled from military service.

title: Base fitness standards on job, not gender or race
proposal: Military physical fitness requirements should depend on the job field, without considering gender, race, ethnicity, or orientation.
quote: Physical fitness requirements should be based on the occupational field without consideration of gender, race, ethnicity, or orientation.

title: Strengthen protections for military chaplains
proposal: Protections should be strengthened so military chaplains can minister according to their faith.
quote: Strengthen protections for chaplains to carry out their ministry according to the tenets of their faith.

title: Put in law that top officers' main duty is readiness
proposal: Law should tell three- and four-star officers that their main duty is military readiness, not a 'social engineering agenda,' reinforced during Senate confirmation.
quote: Codify language to instruct senior military officers (three and four stars) to make certain that they understand their primary duty

title: Reinstate troops discharged over the COVID vaccine
proposal: Service members discharged for refusing the COVID vaccine should be returned to active duty with their rank restored and back pay.
quote: Reinstate servicemembers to active duty who were discharged for not receiving the COVID vaccine, restore their appropriate rank, and provide back pay.

title: Abolish military DEI offices and critical race theory programs
proposal: DOD should end what the chapter calls Marxist and critical race theory programs and abolish new diversity, equity, and inclusion offices and staff.
quote: Eliminate Marxist indoctrination and divisive critical race theory programs and abolish newly established diversity, equity, and inclusion offices and staff.

title: Limit official military social media to recruiting
proposal: Official military social media should be used only for recruiting, and personnel who use command accounts to argue with civilian critics should be disciplined.
quote: Restrict the use of social media solely for purposes of recruitment and discipline any armed services personnel who use an official command channel

title: Audit military academy courses and end faculty tenure
proposal: Military academy courses should be audited to remove what the chapter calls Marxist indoctrination, and tenure for academy professors should be eliminated.
quote: Audit the course offerings at military academies to remove Marxist indoctrination, eliminate tenure for academic professionals

title: End military funding for transgender surgeries and abortion
proposal: Public money should no longer pay for transgender surgeries or help service members obtain abortions.
quote: the use of public monies for transgender surgeries or to facilitate abortion for servicemembers should be ended.

title: Raise pay and family allowances for enlisted troops
proposal: The administration should support legislation to raise wages and family allowances for active-duty enlisted personnel so none need food stamps or housing aid.
quote: Support legislation to increase wages and family allowances for active

title: Improve base housing and consider families in moves
proposal: Military base housing should be improved, and families' needs should be considered when service members are reassigned to new stations.
quote: Improve base housing and consider the military family holistically when considering change-of-station moves.

title: Help military spouses find work and expand childcare
proposal: DOD should improve job opportunities and protections for military spouses, including professional licensing reform, and expand childcare.
quote: Improve spouse employment opportunities and protections, including licensing reform

title: Audit curricula and health policies in DOD schools
proposal: All curricula and health policies in Defense Department schools for military families should be audited, with inappropriate materials removed and policies reversed.
quote: Audit all curricula and health policies in DOD schools for military families, remove all inappropriate materials, and reverse inappropriate policies.

title: Education savings accounts for military families
proposal: The administration should support legislation giving military families the option of education savings accounts.
quote: Support legislation giving education savings account options to military families.

title: Reduce the number of generals and limit their advancement
proposal: The President should limit further promotion of many current senior officers, saying there are too many generals and some were promoted for reasons other than warfighting.
quote: The next President should limit the continued advancement of many of the existing cadre

title: Defense intelligence chief to give top-line and dissenting views
proposal: The Under Secretary of Defense for Intelligence and Security should provide top-line, dissenting, or clarifying views on intelligence assessments, with a larger leadership role.
quote: the Under Secretary of Defense for Intelligence and Security should provide a top-line, dissenting, or clarifying view of DIE and IC assessments as needed.

title: Focus intelligence collection on China and Russia
proposal: Defense intelligence collection and analysis should be aligned with countering China and Russia.
quote: Align collection and analysis with vital national interests (countering China and Russia).

title: Stop duplicate data purchases; invest in AI for intelligence
proposal: Defense intelligence agencies should stop separately buying the same public data and should invest more in machine learning and AI.
quote: We must end the practice of multiple DIE organizations paying to acquire the same PAI data and invest more in machine learning

title: Separate Cyber Command from the NSA
proposal: The shared leadership ('dual-hat') of the National Security Agency and U.S. Cyber Command should be reevaluated; the chapter later says to separate them as Congress directed.
quote: We must reevaluate the dual-hat structure between the National Security Agency (NSA) and U.S. Cyber Command (USCYBERCOM).

title: Rebuild economic analysis, HUMINT and counterintelligence
proposal: Defense intelligence should restore economic analysis to counter China and rebuild human intelligence and counterintelligence, linking them with cyber operations.
quote: Rebuild human intelligence (HUMINT) and counterintelligence (CI) and improve their integration with defensive and offensive cyber operations.

title: Align DOD and DHS on infrastructure and border defense
proposal: DOD and DHS intelligence work should be aligned to better defend critical infrastructure and the border.
quote: Establish true alignment between DOD and DHS both to improve the defense of critical U.S. infrastructure and national border integrity

title: End the 'customer-based' intelligence model
proposal: The administration should end the 'customer is always right' approach to intelligence and enforce procedures that guarantee independent analysis, even if it challenges policymakers.
quote: The next Administration should eliminate the conflict of interest in the current customer-based model (in which the customer is always right)

title: Give defense intelligence a bigger voice in policy
proposal: Defense intelligence should have a larger voice in national policy, matching its share of the intelligence budget, and present views on its own or in joint estimates.
quote: Elevate the DIE’s voice in national policy discussions, commensurate with the DIE’s 75 percent share of the IC budget.

title: Return civilian background checks from DOD to OPM
proposal: Security clearance and suitability investigations for civilian federal workers should move from DOD's Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency back to OPM, except military investigations.
quote: This function should be returned to OPM except for military security clearance investigations.

title: Increase the Army budget, including training
proposal: The Army's budget should be increased so it remains the world's top land power, including more money for training and readiness.
quote: Increase the Army budget to remain the world’s preeminent land power.

title: Speed up the Army's six modernization priorities
proposal: The Army should speed development and purchase of its six modernization priorities, such as long-range fires and air and missile defense.
quote: Accelerate the development and procurement of the six current Army modernization priorities

title: Add 50,000 soldiers to the Army
proposal: The Army's force structure should grow by 50,000 so it can handle two major regional conflicts at once.
quote: Increase the Army force structure by 50,000 to handle two major regional contingencies simultaneously.

title: Boost Army munitions and spare parts production
proposal: The Army should immediately increase production and stockpiles of critical munitions and repair parts.
quote: Immediately increase the production and stockpiling of critical munitions and repair parts.

title: Prioritize Army expeditionary logistics
proposal: The Army should put expeditionary logistics first in force design and planning, train more on joint logistics, and prepare to deploy from damaged U.S. infrastructure.
quote: Prioritize expeditionary logistics in all force design and operational planning to guarantee entry into a contested theater of war.

title: Stop using the Army for social policy
proposal: The Army should stop being used as a 'test bed for social evolution' and refocus on its warfighting mission.
quote: Stop using the Army as a test bed for social evolution.

title: Avoid back-to-back National Guard deployments
proposal: The way the National Guard is used in long operations short of war should change to avoid back-to-back federal and state deployments of the same soldiers.
quote: Transform how the National Guard is employed during extended operations short of declared war to preclude back-to-back federal and state deployments

title: Refocus Army schools on large-scale war with a peer
proposal: Army school curricula should focus on preparing for large-scale land operations against a peer enemy.
quote: Revamp Army school curricula to concentrate on preparation for large

title: Address causes of rising Army suicides
proposal: The Army should address the underlying causes of rising suicide rates among soldiers.
quote: Address the underlying causal issues driving increasing Army suicide rates

title: Build a Navy of more than 355 ships
proposal: The Navy should grow to more than 355 ships and add unmanned systems to support manned forces.
quote: Build a fleet of more than 355 ships.

title: Make range and lethality key in Navy purchases
proposal: Range and lethality should be the main factors in buying and maintaining ships, aircraft, and munitions.
quote: Require that range and lethality be the key factors in all procurement and sustainment decisions for ships, aircraft, and munitions.

title: Reestablish the Navy General Board
proposal: The Navy should recreate a General Board, modeled on the one between the World Wars, with final authority over requirements for ships and shipboard systems.
quote: The interwar General Board should serve as a model, empowered with final decision authority over all requirements documents concerning ships

title: Create a Navy Rapid Capabilities Office
proposal: The Navy should set up a Rapid Capabilities Office, modeled on the Space Development Agency, to field 'good enough' technology quickly under a senior oversight board.
quote: Establish a Rapid Capabilities Office. The USN must transition technology into warfighting capability more rapidly.

title: Produce Navy munitions at maximum rate
proposal: Key naval munitions should be produced at the maximum rate, working with Congress to strengthen supply chains and the workforce.
quote: Produce key munitions at the maximum rate with significant capacity.

title: Require war games and warfighting qualifications for Navy promotions
proposal: The Navy should require warfighting qualifications and war-game participation for career milestones and strengthen the staff office for warfighter development (N7).
quote: Require that war games be utilized as experiential learning environments for the participants as a prerequisite for achieving career milestones

title: Adopt a two-war force-sizing strategy
proposal: The defense strategy should be sized to fight two wars, with scenarios for each service that set the Air Force's resource needs.
quote: Adopt a two-war force defense strategy with scenarios for each service

title: End 'pass-through' funding in the Air Force budget
proposal: Money listed in the Air Force budget that goes to other agencies ('pass-through' funding, over $40 billion a year) should be eliminated.
quote: Eliminate pass-through funding, which has grown to more than $40 billion per year

title: Raise the Air Force budget 5% a year above inflation
proposal: The Air Force budget should grow 5 percent each year after inflation to rebuild its size, age, and readiness.
quote: Increase the Air Force budget by 5 percent annually (after adjusting for inflation)

title: Buy more F-35A fighters and B-21 bombers
proposal: The Air Force should buy 60–80 F-35A fighters a year and build capacity to produce 15–18 B-21 bombers a year.
quote: Increase F-35A procurement to 60–80 per year. 2. Build the capacity for a B-21 production rate of 15–18 aircraft per year

title: Expand Air Force airlift and refueling
proposal: The Air Force should add airlift and aerial refueling capacity to support dispersed operations in Europe and the Pacific.
quote: Increase Air Force airlift and aerial refueling capacity to support agile combat employment operations

title: Buy more mid-range weapons for stealth aircraft
proposal: The Air Force should develop and buy larger numbers of advanced mid-range weapons for stealth aircraft.
quote: Develop and buy larger quantities of advanced mid-range weapons

title: Speed up the Sentinel ICBM
proposal: Development and production of the Sentinel intercontinental ballistic missile should be accelerated to replace the aging Minuteman III.
quote: Accelerate the development and production of the Sentinel intercontinental ballistic missile to reduce the risk inherent in an aging Minuteman III force

title: Double EC-37B electronic warfare aircraft
proposal: The number of EC-37B electronic warfare planes should increase from 10 to 20.
quote: Increase the number of EC-37B electronic warfare aircraft from 10 to 20

title: Invest in next-generation Air Force systems
proposal: The Air Force should field an advanced battle management system, a next-generation air dominance system, moving-target strike capability, and resilient bases and communications.
quote: Attain an operationally optimized advanced battle management system as the Air Force element of the DOD Joint All Domain Command and Control enterprise.

title: Fund an electromagnetic spectrum recovery plan
proposal: The Air Force should create and fund a plan to rebuild its electromagnetic spectrum (electronic warfare) operations after years of neglect.
quote: Establish a vigorous and sufficiently funded electromagnetic spectrum operations recovery plan

title: Eliminate Marine Corps law enforcement battalions
proposal: As part of the Force Design 2030 changes, all Marine Corps law enforcement battalions should be eliminated.
quote: Transform USMC force structure. a. Eliminate all USMC law enforcement battalions.

title: Create Marine Littoral Regiments and shrink infantry battalions
proposal: At least one Marine infantry regiment should become a Marine Littoral Regiment, and remaining infantry battalions should be made smaller.
quote: Transform at least one Marine Infantry Regiment into a Marine Littoral Regiment. c. Reduce the size of remaining infantry battalions.

title: Keep Marine tanks gone and cut most tube artillery
proposal: The Marines should keep their M1 Abrams tanks divested, eliminate most M777 tube artillery batteries, and reduce amphibious assault vehicles.
quote: Maintain divestment of M1 Abrams tanks. b. Eliminate the majority of tube artillery (M777) batteries.

title: Use savings for rockets, drones and missiles for the Marines
proposal: Money freed by cutting older systems should pay for more HIMARS rocket batteries, light armored vehicles, drones and anti-air systems, long-range and anti-ship missiles, and new infantry gear.
quote: Use funds made available by divestment of systems to support new systems that are geared to the likely needs of future conflicts.

title: Match Marine squad leader ranks to the Army's
proposal: Marine combat arms ranks should match the Army's, with E-6s as squad leaders and E-7s as platoon sergeants.
quote: Align the USMC’s combat arms rank structure with the U.S. Army’s (squad leader billets are for E-6s

title: Better incentives to keep junior Marine NCOs
proposal: The Marines should offer better incentives to keep talented junior noncommissioned officers and reduce unnecessary deployments to allow more education.
quote: Create better incentives to retain talented junior NCOs, especially in infantry and other critical military occupational specialties.

title: Build light amphibious warships
proposal: The Navy should develop and build light amphibious warships for more spread-out Marine operations, especially in the Pacific.
quote: Develop and produce light amphibious warships (LAWs) to support more distributed amphibious operations, especially in the Pacific.

title: Keep 28 to 31 large amphibious warships
proposal: The Navy should keep 28 to 31 large amphibious warships instead of the 25 in current plans.
quote: Maintain between 28 and 31 larger amphibious warships as opposed to the 25 specified in current Navy shipbuilding plans

title: Restore offensive space weapons capabilities
proposal: The Space Force should rebuild offensive capabilities, balance offense and defense, and end the study phase by issuing guidance to develop and field offensive systems.
quote: Reestablish offensive capabilities to guarantee a favorable balance of forces, efficiently manage the full deterrence spectrum

title: Expand space control out to the Moon
proposal: The Space Force should quickly expand its space control capability to include cis-lunar space (out to the Moon) to give early warning of attack.
quote: Rapidly expand space control capability, to include cis-lunar space

title: Limit space arms control deals
proposal: The U.S. should seek space arms control or 'rules of the road' only when clearly in U.S. and allied interests and should not follow them unilaterally.
quote: Seek arms control and “rules of the road” understandings only when they are unambiguously in the interests of the U.S. and its allies, and prohibit their unilateral implementation.

title: Declassify information on space threats
proposal: The Space Force should declassify suitable information about rival capabilities that threaten U.S. satellites to justify countering them.
quote: Declassify appropriate information about terrestrial and on-orbit space capabilities that threaten the U.S. space constellation

title: Move Space Force to 'unity of command'
proposal: The Space Force should restructure from a 'unity of effort' arrangement to a 'unity of command' structure.
quote: Restructure from the current “unity of effort” structure to “unity of command.”

title: Declare the U.S. will operate at will in space
proposal: The Space Force should lead creation of a clear U.S. policy that the country will operate freely in space and enforce that with deterrent capabilities.
quote: Lead the U.S. government’s development of a clear and unambiguous declaratory policy that the United States will operate at will in space

title: Change the Space Development Agency's 'fail-early' approach
proposal: The Space Development Agency should keep fast timelines but use much more engineering rigor instead of its 'fail-early' approach.
quote: Alter the Space Development Agency’s current “fail-early” approach and transition to a methodology that maintains aggressive timelines

title: Add more Space Force general officers
proposal: The number of Space Force general officer positions should increase so it can compete for resources equally with other services.
quote: Increase the number of general officer positions to ensure the Space Force’s ability to compete for resources

title: Explore creating a Space Force Academy
proposal: DOD should explore a Space Force Academy, first attached to a major research university and later built as its own service academy.
quote: Explore creation of a Space Force Academy to attract top aero–astro students, engineers, and scientists and develop astronauts.

title: Expand offensive and defensive cyber operations
proposal: Cyber Command should conduct offensive cyber operations and expand defensive cyber operations authorized under Trump's National Security Presidential Memorandum 13.
quote: Expand defensive cyber-effects operations authorized by President Trump's classified National Security Presidential Memorandum 13

title: End Cyber Command's role in election security
proposal: Cyber Command should stop taking part in federal efforts to 'fortify' U.S. elections, to avoid the appearance of partisan politics.
quote: End USCYBERCOM’s participation in federal efforts to “fortify” U.S. elections to eliminate the perception that DOD is engaging in partisan politics.

title: Merge cyber and electronic warfare; push cyber authority lower
proposal: Cyber and electronic warfare doctrine should be integrated, and cyber authorities should no longer be held only at the strategic level.
quote: Accelerate the integration of cyber and electronic warfare (EW) doctrine and capabilities

title: Adopt GAO advice on cyber incident reporting
proposal: DOD should follow a GAO recommendation to align policies so it has department-wide visibility of cyber incident reports.
quote: Implement the Government Accountability Office’s recommendation that the DOD Chief Information Officer, Commander of USCYBERCOM

title: Define DOD cyber roles in the National Security Strategy
proposal: The October 2022 National Security Strategy should be updated to define DOD's cyber roles and responsibilities more concretely.
quote: Update the October 2022 National Security Strategy to define DOD roles and responsibilities beyond existing platitudes.

title: Retaliate against foreign cyberattacks
proposal: The U.S. should apply traditional deterrence to cyber, using cyber and electronic warfare to retaliate against foreign cyberattacks on U.S. infrastructure and people.
quote: Apply traditional deterrence strategies and principles for using cyber/ EW in retaliation for foreign cyberattacks

title: Broadly redefine irregular warfare
proposal: Irregular warfare should be redefined to cover using all elements of national power against state rivals and nonstate actors, and threats should be described by region in the National Security Strategy.
quote: Define irregular warfare as “a means by which the United States uses all elements of national power to project influence abroad to counter state adversaries

title: Put irregular warfare in the National Defense Strategy, led by SOCOM
proposal: Irregular warfare should be built directly into the National Defense Strategy, with U.S. Special Operations Command named lead for irregular warfare against hostile actors.
quote: Direct that irregular warfare resources, capabilities, and strategies be incorporated directly into the overall National Defense Strategy

title: Create an Irregular Warfare Center of Excellence
proposal: DOD should set up an Irregular Warfare Center of Excellence to help train and organize forces for irregular warfare.
quote: Establish an Irregular Warfare Center of Excellence to help DOD train, equip, and organize to conduct irregular warfare

title: Task Special Operations with countering China's Belt and Road
proposal: Special Operations Command and Pentagon offices should plan and carry out regional operations to counter China's Belt and Road Initiative in key countries.
quote: Task USSOCOM and corresponding organizations in the Pentagon with conceptualizing, resourcing, and executing regionally based operations to counter the BRI

title: Publicize Chinese violations through information operations
proposal: The U.S. should use information operations to highlight Chinese violations of economic zones and human rights and its coercion and use of sovereign debt.
quote: Use regional and global information operations to highlight Chinese violations of Exclusive Economic Zones, violations of human rights

title: Counter Chinese economic power in the Western Hemisphere
proposal: The U.S. should use all elements of national power to counter Chinese economic power in North America, Central America, and the Caribbean.
quote: Directly counter Chinese economic power with all elements of national power in North America, Central America, and the Caribbean

title: 'Name and shame' those who target democratic processes
proposal: The U.S. should publicly release the names of entities that target democratic processes and international norms.
quote: Employ a “name and shame” approach by making information regarding the names of entities that target democratic processes and international norms available

title: Use economic warfare and lawfare against hostile actors
proposal: DOD should work with other agencies to use economic warfare, legal action, and diplomatic pressure against hostile state and nonstate actors.
quote: Work with the Interagency to employ economic warfare, lawfare, and diplomatic pressure against hostile state and nonstate actors.

title: Accelerate nuclear triad modernization
proposal: Timelines should be sped up for the Sentinel missile, Long Range Standoff Weapon, Columbia-class submarine, B-21 bomber, and nuclear-capable F-35.
quote: Accelerate the timelines of critical modernization programs including the Sentinel missile, Long Range Standoff Weapon (LRSO), Columbia-class ballistic missile submarine

title: Reject extending the Minuteman III's life
proposal: The administration should oppose congressional proposals to further extend the service life of older systems such as the Minuteman III missile.
quote: Reject any congressional proposals that would further extend the service lives of U.S. capabilities such as the Minuteman III ICBM.

title: Fully fund nuclear warhead life extension programs
proposal: Enough money should be provided for warhead life extension programs, including the B61-12, W80-4, W87-1 Mod, and W88 Alt 370.
quote: Ensure sufficient funding for warhead life extension programs (LEP), including the B61-12, W80-4, W87-1 Mod, and W88 Alt 370.

title: Restore the nuclear sea-launched cruise missile (SLCM-N)
proposal: The President should support and speed funding for the nuclear sea-launched cruise missile, canceled by the Biden administration, aiming to deploy it by the end of the decade.
quote: The next President should support and accelerate funding for development of the SLCM-N with the goal of deployment by the end of the decade.

title: Consider more nuclear weapons to deter China
proposal: The U.S. should consider buying more Sentinel missiles or LRSOs than planned, improve its ability to upload extra warheads in a crisis, and review new capabilities to deter China.
quote: Consider procuring more modernized nuclear systems (such as the Sentinel missile or LRSO) than currently planned.

title: Restore plutonium pit production and nuclear infrastructure
proposal: The U.S. should speed up restoring plutonium pit production and keep investing in National Laboratory facilities that support nuclear weapons.
quote: Accelerate the effort to restore plutonium pit production, which is essential both for modern warhead programs and for recapitalizing the stockpile.

title: Be ready to resume nuclear weapons testing
proposal: The U.S. should restore its readiness to test nuclear weapons at the Nevada National Security Site.
quote: Restore readiness to test nuclear weapons at the Nevada National Security Site

title: Reject nuclear disarmament proposals that weaken deterrence
proposal: The U.S. should reject disarmament proposals that undercut deterrence and pursue arms control only when it serves U.S. and allied security.
quote: Reject proposals for nuclear disarmament that are contrary to the goal of bolstering deterrence.

title: Keep homeland missile defense out of arms control talks
proposal: The U.S. should commit to never putting homeland missile defense on the table in arms control talks with Russia and China.
quote: Commit to keeping homeland missile defense off the table in any arms control negotiations with Russia and China.

title: Buy at least 64 Next Generation Interceptors
proposal: The U.S. should buy at least 64 Next Generation Interceptors for homeland missile defense, compared with the 20 the Biden administration planned.
quote: Buy at least 64 of the Next Generation Interceptor (NGI), which is more advanced than the GBI, for an eventual uniform fleet of interceptors.

title: Consider an East Coast missile interceptor site
proposal: The U.S. should consider more steps to strengthen homeland missile defense, such as layered defense or a third interceptor site on the East Coast.
quote: Consider additional steps to strengthen the GMD system such as a layered missile defense or a third interceptor site on the East Coast.

title: Buy more THAAD, SM-3 and Patriot missile defenses
proposal: The U.S. should prioritize buying more regional missile defense systems such as THAAD, Standard Missile-3, and Patriot.
quote: The U.S. should prioritize procurement of more regional defense systems such as Theater High Altitude Area Defense (THAAD), Standard Missile-3, and Patriot missiles.

title: Defend the homeland against Russian and Chinese missiles
proposal: The U.S. should drop its policy of not defending the homeland against Russian and Chinese ballistic missiles and work to improve those defenses.
quote: Abandon the existing policy of not defending the homeland against Russian and Chinese ballistic missiles

title: Invest in directed-energy and space-based missile defense
proposal: The U.S. should invest in future missile defense technologies such as directed energy and space-based defenses.
quote: Invest in future advanced missile defense technologies like directed energy or space-based missile defense

title: Defend against cruise and hypersonic missiles
proposal: The U.S. should invest in homeland cruise missile defense, speed up space-based sensors to track non-ballistic missiles, and accelerate the Glide Phase Interceptor against hypersonic weapons.
quote: Accelerate the program to deploy space-based sensors that can detect and track missiles flying on nonballistic trajectories.
